rows.comment: Two files declare `package Shared::Thing`. `from_alpha` is defined in Alpha.pm, but the name-keyed module cache holds ONE winner per package name (`cache.insert` is last-write-wins, and `purge_module` drops the loser's edges), so goto-def lands in Beta.pm. This is a WRONG answer, not a missing one — the user is navigated confidently to the wrong file. The fix is the name->candidates relation Perl lacks and the pack tier already has (`all_defs`), scoped by what the asker can see.

`Alpha::Second` is the SECOND package declared in Alpha.pm. Registration keys on `first_package_name`, so every package after the first gets no name entry and is unreachable by name. Multi-package .pm files are ordinary Perl, so this is a common shape, not an exotic one.

The method twin of pkgid-01: `Shared::Widget` is declared in Widget.pm (holding `new`/`base_method`) AND WidgetExtra.pm (holding `extra_method`, loaded dynamically — the asker never `use`s it by file name, so no name-keyed @INC entry compensates). `$w->extra_method` must land in WidgetExtra.pm — the winner-keyed class lookup (`get_cached(class)` in the ancestry walk and the goto-def consumer) can only see one file's methods, so the losing file's method misses or misleads depending on registration order. Method resolution over a reopened package is ordinary OO Perl.
Control for pkgid-04: the class's main file's own method keeps resolving after the candidate-set change.
The control for the two xfails above: the package-name winner must keep resolving. A fix that introduces candidate sets has to keep this correct, not trade one wrong answer for another.
